harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL7) serving AMQP strictly over TLS on port 5671 with mutual TLS enforced against a cluster-dedicated CA, and restricted the management UI (15672) to the cluster-internal network. Erlang 28.5.0.5 and RabbitMQ 4.3.5 were installed from the official zero-dependency EL7 GitHub release RPMs (RHEL7 had no configured yum repos and upstream no longer ships EL7 packages/repo). A private CA was generated on node1 with per-node server certs (SAN=hostname+cluster IP) and a client cert; rabbitmq.conf disables plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp = none), enables listeners.ssl on 5671 with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, and binds management.tcp.ip to each node's private cluster IP (10.100.9.x) with firewalld further restricting 15672/25672/4369 to the 10.100.9.0/24 subnet. All 3 nodes clustered automatically via classic_config peer discovery sharing one Erlang cookie. Verified: TLS connections without a client cert or with a non-CA (rogue) cert are rejected at the handshake; a CA-issued client cert completes the handshake and receives a real AMQP Connection.Start frame; a full publish/get message round-trip succeeded via the management API. Also fixed significant clock drift (~9 days) on all 3 nodes via chrony/date, which was blocking TLS cert validation for package downloads. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified RabbitMQ became active, full 3/3 cluster quorum returned, and TLS/mTLS enforcement plus message publish/consume worked after each restart, before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes (RHEL7, no yum repos, no rabbitmq/erlang installed)
Diagnosed and fixed ~9-day clock drift on all nodes via chronyd stop/date -s/hwclock/chronyd start (blocked TLS cert validation for downloads)
Downloaded and installed zero-dependency erlang-28.5.0.5-1.el7.x86_64.rpm and rabbitmq-server-4.3.5-1.el8.noarch.rpm on all 3 nodes
Set up passwordless inter-node SSH using CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY and populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS
Generated a dedicated CA (4096-bit RSA, 10y) on node1, plus per-node server certs (SAN=hostname+IP) and a CA-issued client cert; also generated a rogue self-signed cert for negative testing
Distributed CA cert + per-node server cert/key to /etc/rabbitmq/tls on each node via scp/ssh, with correct ownership/permissions
Synced a shared Erlang cookie to all 3 nodes for clustering

Wrote rabbitmq.conf on each node: listeners.tcp=none, listeners.ssl.default=5671 with verify_peer+fail_if_no_peer_cert, management.tcp.ip bound to each node's private cluster IP, classic_config peer discovery listing all 3 nodes
Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin (offline) on all 3 nodes
Configured firewalld: opened 5671/tcp broadly for AMQP TLS clients; restricted 15672 (management), 25672 (clustering), 4369 (epmd) to source 10.100.9.0/24 only
Started rabbitmq-server on all 3 nodes; verified automatic cluster formation (3/3 running nodes, no partitions)
Verified mTLS enforcement: no-cert and rogue-cert connections fail TLS handshake; CA-issued client cert succeeds and receives a genuine AMQP Connection.Start frame
Created a non-default management admin user (cluster_admin) and verified management API is reachable from another cluster node but bound only to the private IP (not 0.0.0.0)
Performed an end-to-end publish/get message test via the management API to prove broker functionality

Executed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline on all nodes, rebooted node1 then node2 then node3 sequentially (never concurrently), polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed each time, and re-verified RabbitMQ active + 3/3 cluster quorum + TLS/mTLS enforcement (and a post-restart message round-trip) after each restart before proceeding to the next node

evidence.requirement: 3-node RabbitMQ cluster formed across node1/node2/node3
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all 3 nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching RabbitMQ/Erlang versions, no partitions

evidence.requirement: AMQP served only over TLS (no plaintext listener)
evidence.summary: ss -tlnp on node1 shows only :::5671 for AMQP; no 5672 listener present, confirming listeners.tcp=none took effect

evidence.requirement: Only CA-issued client certificates are accepted for AMQP TLS connections
evidence.summary: openssl s_client tests on 5671: connection without any client cert fails with SSL handshake failure alert; connection with a rogue non-CA cert fails with bad certificate alert; connection with the CA-issued client cert completes with Verify return code 0

evidence.requirement: AMQP over TLS is functionally operational for CA-authenticated clients
evidence.summary: Raw AMQP protocol header sent over the mTLS session returns a genuine server Connection.Start frame; a full publish/get message round trip via the broker succeeded

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: Management (15672) is bound only to the node's private cluster IP (10.100.9.10), not 0.0.0.0, and firewalld additionally restricts 15672/25672/4369 to the 10.100.9.0/24 subnet; node2 successfully reached node1's management API using its cluster IP, proving in-cluster reachability

evidence.requirement: CA created specifically for this cluster
evidence.summary: Generated a dedicated CA cert/key and issued per-node server certs plus a client cert signed by that CA

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 3dba43a5...; reboot acknowledged via connection closed by remote host; post-reboot boot_id changed to c144037d...; rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows 3/3 nodes running again; TLS handshake still requires the CA client cert

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 738d0aac...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 1078e434...; cluster_status shows 3/3 nodes running; mTLS re-verified against node2's IP from node1 with Verify return code 0

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2fc81aed...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to 329346af...; cluster_status shows 3/3 nodes running; TLS enforcement re-verified (no-cert rejected, CA cert accepted) against node3's IP

evidence.requirement: Full post-restart functional verification of the cluster (final state)
evidence.summary: After all three restarts, a fresh publish/get message round trip succeeded via the management API and 15672 remained bound only to the private cluster IP
